key_insight: Halcyon shows that strong text-to-image generation does not require language pretraining. Trained from scratch, Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 while using 18.2× less pretraining compute.
problem_solved: Modern text-to-image systems typically rely on internet-scale language pretraining. This work tests whether models can generate high-quality images from text without that dependency.
method: Introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models.
Pretrain entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100 million image-text pairs.
Compare generation quality and pretraining compute: Halcyon-0.52B achieves 48.0 gFD versus LlamaGen-XL/8's 63.3, where lower is better.
impact: The results suggest a more compute-efficient route to text-to-image modeling without a pretrained language backbone. Practitioners gain evidence that paired image-text training alone can support strong generation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: 100M image-text pairs → early-fusion Halcyon trained from scratch → generated images.
Bar chart comparing gFD: Halcyon-0.52B at 48.0 versus LlamaGen-XL/8 at 63.3, labeled 'lower is better.'
Compute comparison graphic highlighting 18.2× less pretraining compute than LlamaGen-XL/8.
Side-by-side workflow icons contrasting language-pretrained systems with Halcyon's from-scratch approach.
paper_title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
paper_authors: Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Yue Zhao, Armin W. Thomas, Ehsan Adeli, Jiajun Wu
